You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

**Execution Date: August 18, 2023**

This Agreement resolves all disputes between the Parties in connection with *Cardinal Peak Industries v. Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.*, Case No. 2022-L-008471, Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, County Department, Law Division

This Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (this \"**Agreement**\") is entered into as of August 18, 2023 (the \"**Effective Date**\"), by and between:

**Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 4200 West Lakeshore Industrial Parkway, Suite 300, Waukegan, Illinois 60085 (EIN: 36-4821097; Delaware Charter No. 7284159) (hereinafter \"**Nexford**\" or \"**NIH**\");

and

**Cardinal Peak Industries**, a Colorado limited liability company with its principal place of business at 1580 Ridgeline Boulevard, Pueblo, Colorado 81001 (EIN: 84-3295618) (hereinafter \"**Cardinal Peak**\" or \"**CPI**\").

Nexford and Cardinal Peak are each referred to individually herein as a \"**Party**\" and collectively as the \"**Parties**.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, Nexford and Cardinal Peak are parties to that certain Master Supply Agreement dated January 15, 2020, designated MSA-NIH-CPI-2020-001 (the \"**MSA**\"), pursuant to which Cardinal Peak manufactures and supplies hot-rolled coil (\"**HRC**\") and cold-rolled coil (\"**CRC**\") steel products to Nexford for use in Nexford\'s downstream fabrication and distribution operations;

**WHEREAS**, the MSA provides for the pass-through of certain raw-material surcharges, including scrap surcharges, energy surcharges, and alloy surcharges, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in Section 7.4 of the MSA and the methodology prescribed in Exhibit C thereto (the \"**Surcharge Methodology**\"), which methodology specifies, among other things, the applicable indices, baseline reference points, calculation periods, and cap-and-collar mechanisms governing the determination of such surcharges;

**WHEREAS**, a dispute arose between the Parties concerning surcharge invoices issued by Cardinal Peak for the period from March 2021 through May 2022 (the \"**Disputed Period**\"), during which Cardinal Peak invoiced total surcharges of approximately Six Million Four Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars (\$6,410,000.00), of which Nexford paid One Million Six Hundred Eighty Thousand Dollars (\$1,680,000.00), and Cardinal Peak claims an unpaid balance of approximately Four Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$4,730,000.00) (the \"**Surcharge Dispute**\");

**WHEREAS**, at the core of the Surcharge Dispute, Nexford contends that Cardinal Peak deviated from the Surcharge Methodology by, among other things, utilizing incorrect index reference dates, applying surcharges to product categories excluded from the surcharge pass-through framework, and failing to apply the cap-and-collar limitations set forth in Exhibit C, while Cardinal Peak contends that its surcharge calculations were proper and in accordance with the MSA as reasonably interpreted;

**WHEREAS**, on June 10, 2022, Cardinal Peak, through its counsel Blackwood Stein & Associates LLP, issued a formal demand to Nexford for payment of Four Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$4,730,000.00), which demand included a detailed reconciliation of surcharge invoices for the Disputed Period, and Nexford, through its General Counsel Deborah Whitfield, rejected such demand by letter dated July 5, 2022, setting forth Nexford\'s position that a substantial portion of the surcharges had been improperly calculated;

**WHEREAS**, on August 8, 2022, Cardinal Peak filed a Complaint against Nexford in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, County Department, Law Division, docketed as Case No. 2022-L-008471 (the \"**Litigation**\"), asserting claims for breach of contract (Count I), unjust enrichment (Count II), and account stated (Count III), and seeking damages in the amount of \$4,730,000.00, plus pre-judgment interest, costs, and attorneys\' fees;

**WHEREAS**, on September 19, 2022, Nexford, through its counsel Calderwood & Harkness LLP, filed an Answer and Affirmative Defenses to the Complaint, raising, among other defenses, failure to comply with contractual conditions precedent, failure to mitigate, estoppel, and the contractual cap-and-collar limitations, and on October 3, 2022, Nexford filed a Counterclaim (the \"**Counterclaim**\") asserting breach of contract by Cardinal Peak and seeking declaratory judgment that Cardinal Peak\'s surcharge calculations were inconsistent with the Surcharge Methodology, as well as recovery of alleged overpayments in the approximate amount of Two Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars (\$210,000.00);

**WHEREAS**, the Parties have engaged in extensive discovery in the Litigation, including the exchange of thousands of pages of documents, interrogatory responses, and requests for admission, as well as depositions of fact witnesses and the exchange of expert reports addressing the proper interpretation and application of the Surcharge Methodology, and have thereby fully informed themselves of the facts and law relating to the Surcharge Dispute;

**WHEREAS**, the MSA, at Section 14.3, provides for mandatory mediation in Chicago, Illinois, administered by a mutually agreed-upon neutral mediator, as a prerequisite to the continuation of litigation, and on May 22, 2023, the Parties jointly moved to stay the Litigation pending mediation, which motion was granted by the Honorable Judge Raymond P. Callahan on June 5, 2023;

**WHEREAS**, on August 2, 2023, the Parties participated in a full-day mediation session before the Honorable Catherine Lindström (Ret.) at the Great Lakes Dispute Resolution Center, 150 North Riverside Plaza, Suite 2700, Chicago, Illinois 60606, at which session the Parties, after extensive arms-length negotiation, reached an agreement in principle to resolve the Surcharge Dispute, the material terms of which were memorialized in a term sheet signed by authorized representatives of both Parties on August 2, 2023 (the \"**Term Sheet**\");

**WHEREAS**, the Parties desire to fully and finally resolve and settle the Litigation, including all claims asserted in the Complaint and the Counterclaim, and all other disputes, claims, and controversies between them arising out of or relating to the MSA, the Surcharge Dispute, and the Disputed Period, without any admission of liability, wrongdoing, or fault by either Party, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement;

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged by each Party, the Parties hereby agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE 1 --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article 1 shall have the meanings given to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

**1.1 \"Agreement\"** means this Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, including all exhibits and schedules attached hereto, as the same may be amended or supplemented from time to time in accordance with Section 9.4 hereof.

**1.2 \"Cardinal Peak Released Parties\"** means Cardinal Peak Industries, together with its members, managers, officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, affiliates, subsidiaries, successors, and assigns, including without limitation the following individuals in their individual and corporate capacities: Frank Delacroix, Natalie Gunderson, Harold Briggs, and Patricia Morrow.

**1.3 \"Counterclaim\"** means the Counterclaim filed by Nexford on October 3, 2022 in the Litigation, including all claims for breach of contract, declaratory relief, and recovery of alleged overpayments asserted therein, and any amendments thereto.

**1.4 \"Disputed Period\"** means the period commencing March 1, 2021 and ending May 31, 2022, inclusive.

**1.5 \"Effective Date\"** means August 18, 2023, the date of execution of this Agreement by both Parties.

**1.6 \"Litigation\"** means the lawsuit styled *Cardinal Peak Industries v. Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.*, Case No. 2022-L-008471, pending in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, County Department, Law Division, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, third-party claims, motions, and proceedings filed or initiated therein.

**1.7 \"MSA\"** means the Master Supply Agreement dated January 15, 2020, reference number MSA-NIH-CPI-2020-001, entered into between Nexford and Cardinal Peak, together with all exhibits, schedules, amendments, and addenda thereto.

**1.8 \"Nexford Released Parties\"** means Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc., together with its officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, affiliates (including without limitation Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Partners, LP and Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Management LLC), subsidiaries, successors, and assigns, including without limitation the following individuals in their individual and corporate capacities: Martin Schaeffer, Lydia Tran, Russell Okonkwo, and Deborah Whitfield.

**1.9 \"Settlement Amount\"** means the aggregate sum of One Million Eight Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$1,890,000.00), as further described in Article 2 hereof.

**1.10 \"Term Sheet\"** means the term sheet signed by authorized representatives of both Parties on August 2, 2023, at the conclusion of the mediation session before the Honorable Catherine Lindström (Ret.). Upon execution of this Agreement, the Term Sheet is superseded in its entirety by this Agreement and shall have no further force or effect.

**[ARTICLE 2 --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**2.1 Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, demands, and causes of action asserted or that could have been asserted in the Litigation or otherwise arising out of or relating to the Surcharge Dispute, the MSA (including Section 7.4, Exhibit C, and the Surcharge Methodology), and the Disputed Period, Nexford shall pay to Cardinal Peak the aggregate sum of One Million Eight Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$1,890,000.00) (the \"**Settlement Amount**\"). The Parties acknowledge that the Settlement Amount represents approximately forty percent (40%) of the Four Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$4,730,000.00) claimed by Cardinal Peak in the Litigation and has been negotiated at arms\' length, through mediation, and reflects a compromise of the Parties\' respective claims and defenses. Payment of the Settlement Amount, in accordance with the terms set forth herein, shall constitute full satisfaction of all obligations of Nexford to Cardinal Peak arising out of or relating to the Surcharge Dispute and the Litigation.

**2.2 Payment Schedule.** The Settlement Amount shall be paid by Nexford to Cardinal Peak in two (2) installments, as follows:

> **(a) First Installment.** One Million One Hundred Thirty-Four Thousand Dollars (\$1,134,000.00), representing sixty percent (60%) of the Settlement Amount, shall be due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date, that is, no later than September 17, 2023.
>
> **(b) Second Installment.** Seven Hundred Fifty-Six Thousand Dollars (\$756,000.00), representing forty percent (40%) of the Settlement Amount, shall be due and payable within ninety (90) calendar days of the Effective Date, that is, no later than November 16, 2023.

**2.3 Payment Method.** All payments under this Article 2 shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States Dollars to a bank account designated by Cardinal Peak in writing. Cardinal Peak shall provide Nexford with complete wire transfer instructions, including the name of the receiving bank, ABA routing number, account number, and account name, within five (5) business days of the Effective Date. Nexford shall not be deemed in default of any payment obligation under this Agreement if Cardinal Peak fails to timely provide such wire transfer instructions, in which case the applicable payment deadline shall be extended by one (1) business day for each business day of delay in providing such instructions.

**2.4 Late Payment.** If Nexford fails to make any installment payment when due under Section 2.2, interest shall accrue on the unpaid amount at the rate of eight percent (8%) per annum (compounding monthly) from the date such payment was due until the date such payment is received by Cardinal Peak in full. In addition, if any installment payment remains unpaid for more than ten (10) business days following its due date (after giving effect to any extension under Section 2.3), then the entire remaining unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon, shall become immediately due and payable upon written notice from Cardinal Peak to Nexford. The acceleration remedy provided in this Section 2.4 shall be in addition to, and not in limitation of, any other rights or remedies available to Cardinal Peak at law or in equity, including the right to enforce this Agreement pursuant to Article 4.

**2.5 Tax Treatment.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own tax obligations arising from or relating to the receipt or payment of the Settlement Amount, including without limitation all federal, state, and local income taxes, and neither Party makes any representation to the other regarding the tax consequences of the Settlement Amount. Cardinal Peak shall provide Nexford with a properly completed and executed Internal Revenue Service Form W-9 (Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification) prior to the date on which the First Installment is due. In the event Cardinal Peak fails to provide a completed Form W-9 in a timely manner, Nexford shall be entitled to withhold from any payment such amounts as may be required by applicable tax law.

**[ARTICLE 3 --- MUTUAL RELEASES]{.underline}**

**3.1 Release by Cardinal Peak.** Effective upon receipt by Cardinal Peak of the First Installment payment described in Section 2.2(a), Cardinal Peak, on behalf of itself and each of the Cardinal Peak Released Parties, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, acquits, and forever discharges each of the Nexford Released Parties from any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, specialties, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, promises, variances, trespasses, damages, judgments, extents, executions, losses, costs, expenses (including but not limited to attorneys\' fees and expert witness fees), liabilities, and obligations of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, disclosed or undisclosed, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, accrued or unaccrued, liquidated or unliquidated, at law, in equity, or otherwise, that Cardinal Peak or any Cardinal Peak Released Party ever had, now has, or may hereafter claim to have against any Nexford Released Party, arising out of or in any way relating to:

> \(a\) the MSA, including without limitation Section 7.4 thereof, Exhibit C thereto, and the Surcharge Methodology, as well as all purchase orders, invoices, delivery schedules, change orders, and other documents issued or exchanged pursuant to or in connection with the MSA during the Disputed Period;
>
> \(b\) the Surcharge Dispute, including without limitation all surcharge invoices, surcharge calculations, surcharge reconciliations, and surcharge-related communications between the Parties during the Disputed Period (March 2021 through May 2022);
>
> \(c\) the Litigation, including without limitation all claims asserted in the Complaint filed by Cardinal Peak on August 8, 2022, specifically including the claims for breach of contract (Count I), unjust enrichment (Count II), and account stated (Count III); and
>
> \(d\) any and all other matters, facts, events, transactions, acts, omissions, or circumstances that were or could have been asserted by Cardinal Peak or any Cardinal Peak Released Party in the Litigation, whether or not actually pled, whether arising under statute, common law, contract, tort, or any other theory of recovery.

**3.2 Release by Nexford.** Effective upon execution of this Agreement by both Parties, Nexford, on behalf of itself and each of the Nexford Released Parties, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, acquits, and forever discharges each of the Cardinal Peak Released Parties from any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, specialties, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, promises, variances, trespasses, damages, judgments, extents, executions, losses, costs, expenses (including but not limited to attorneys\' fees and expert witness fees), liabilities, and obligations of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, disclosed or undisclosed, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, accrued or unaccrued, liquidated or unliquidated, at law, in equity, or otherwise, that Nexford or any Nexford Released Party ever had, now has, or may hereafter claim to have against any Cardinal Peak Released Party, arising out of or in any way relating to:

> \(a\) the MSA, including without limitation Section 7.4 thereof, Exhibit C thereto, and the Surcharge Methodology, as well as all purchase orders, invoices, delivery schedules, change orders, and other documents issued or exchanged pursuant to or in connection with the MSA during the Disputed Period;
>
> \(b\) the Surcharge Dispute, including without limitation all surcharge invoices, surcharge calculations, surcharge reconciliations, and surcharge-related communications between the Parties during the Disputed Period;
>
> \(c\) the Counterclaim filed by Nexford on October 3, 2022, including without limitation the claim for recovery of alleged overpayments in the approximate amount of Two Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars (\$210,000.00), the claim for breach of contract, and the request for declaratory relief; and
>
> \(d\) any and all other matters, facts, events, transactions, acts, omissions, or circumstances that were or could have been asserted by Nexford or any Nexford Released Party in the Litigation or the Counterclaim, whether or not actually pled, whether arising under statute, common law, contract, tort, or any other theory of recovery.

**3.3 Unknown Claims Waiver.** Each Party expressly acknowledges and agrees that the releases set forth in Sections 3.1 and 3.2 extend to all claims of every nature and kind whatsoever, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, and whether or not concealed or hidden, that exist as of the Effective Date and that arise out of or relate to the subject matter of the releases set forth herein. Each Party expressly waives and relinquishes, to the fullest extent permitted by law, any rights or benefits that it may have under Section 1542 of the California Civil Code (or any analogous provision of any other state\'s law), which provides:

> *\"A general release does not extend to claims that the creditor or releasing party does not know or suspect to exist in his or her favor at the time of executing the release and that, if known by him or her, would have materially affected his or her settlement with the debtor or released party.\"*

Each Party understands the significance of this waiver of unknown claims and acknowledges that it has been advised by its legal counsel with respect thereto and assumes the risk that facts additional to or different from those that it now knows or believes to be true may later be discovered, and agrees that this Agreement shall be and remain effective in all respects regardless of the discovery of any such additional or different facts.

**3.4 No Admission of Liability.** This Agreement, and the settlement and releases reflected herein, do not constitute and shall not be construed as an admission of liability, wrongdoing, fault, or responsibility by either Party or any of their respective Released Parties. Neither Party admits that any of the claims, counterclaims, defenses, or affirmative defenses asserted in the Litigation have merit or lack merit. This Agreement is entered into solely for the purpose of settling disputed claims and avoiding the uncertainty, expense, and burden of continued litigation. This Agreement, and any statements made or acts performed in connection with the negotiation or execution hereof, shall not be offered or received in evidence in any action or proceeding of any kind as an admission or concession of liability or wrongdoing of any nature, and shall not be admissible for any purpose other than to enforce the terms of this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE 4 --- DISMISSAL OF LITIGATION]{.underline}**

**4.1 Stipulation of Dismissal.** Within five (5) business days following the Effective Date, counsel for the Parties shall jointly prepare, execute, and file with the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, a Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice of all claims and counterclaims pending in the Litigation, Case No. 2022-L-008471, in a form substantially consistent with the requirements of the Illinois Code of Civil Procedure and the local rules of the Circuit Court of Cook County. The Stipulation of Dismissal shall provide that each Party shall bear its own attorneys\' fees, costs, and expenses incurred in connection with the Litigation.

**4.2 Cooperation.** Each Party shall cooperate fully with the other Party, and shall execute and deliver such further documents and instruments as may be reasonably necessary or appropriate, to effectuate the dismissal of the Litigation in accordance with Section 4.1, including without limitation any agreed orders, stipulations, or other filings required by the Court.

**4.3 Court Retention of Jurisdiction.** Notwithstanding the dismissal of the Litigation with prejudice, the Parties agree that the Stipulation of Dismissal shall expressly provide that the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, shall retain jurisdiction solely for the purpose of enforcing the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including but not limited to the payment obligations set forth in Article 2 and the confidentiality obligations set forth in Article 6. Either Party may apply to the Court for enforcement of this Agreement without the necessity of filing a new action or proceeding.

**[ARTICLE 5 --- TERMINATION OF THE MSA]{.underline}**

**5.1 MSA Termination.** The MSA (MSA-NIH-CPI-2020-001, dated January 15, 2020) shall terminate by mutual agreement of the Parties effective as of August 31, 2023 (the \"**MSA Termination Date**\"). Promptly following the execution of this Agreement, and in any event no later than August 25, 2023, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith and execute a separate Mutual Termination Agreement, in form and substance reasonably acceptable to both Parties, to memorialize and effectuate such termination. The Mutual Termination Agreement shall be consistent with, and shall not contradict or modify, the terms of this Agreement.

**5.2 Transition Period.** Notwithstanding the MSA Termination Date, all outstanding purchase orders that have been duly issued by Nexford and accepted by Cardinal Peak in writing prior to the MSA Termination Date shall continue to be fulfilled by Cardinal Peak, and accepted and paid for by Nexford, in accordance with the terms and conditions of the MSA, through and including October 31, 2023 (the \"**Transition Period End Date**\"). During the period from the MSA Termination Date through the Transition Period End Date (the \"**Transition Period**\"), the pricing, delivery, quality, inspection, and warranty terms of the MSA shall remain in full force and effect solely with respect to such outstanding purchase orders. For the avoidance of doubt, no surcharge disputes relating to the Transition Period shall be subject to the releases set forth in Article 3; however, the Parties agree that all surcharge calculations during the Transition Period shall be performed strictly in accordance with the Surcharge Methodology set forth in Exhibit C to the MSA, and any disputes regarding such calculations shall be resolved in accordance with the dispute resolution provisions of the MSA.

**5.3 No New Orders.** Nexford shall not issue, and Cardinal Peak shall have no obligation to accept, any new purchase orders under the MSA on or after the MSA Termination Date. Any purchase order purportedly issued by Nexford under the MSA after August 31, 2023 shall be null and void and of no force or effect.

**5.4 Surviving MSA Provisions.** Notwithstanding the termination of the MSA as provided in this Article 5, the following provisions of the MSA shall survive such termination and shall continue in full force and effect in accordance with their respective terms: indemnification obligations (Section 11.2 of the MSA), limitation of liability (Section 11.4 of the MSA), and confidentiality (Section 12.1 of the MSA), in each case solely to the extent that such provisions relate to obligations, liabilities, or claims arising out of acts or omissions occurring prior to the MSA Termination Date or during the Transition Period. The survival of such provisions shall not be construed to extend or revive any claims released under Article 3 of this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE 6 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**6.1 Confidential Treatment.** The Parties agree that the existence and terms of this Agreement, including without limitation the Settlement Amount, the payment schedule, the nature and scope of the mutual releases, and all related negotiations, mediation proceedings, communications, and documents exchanged in connection therewith, shall be treated as strictly confidential and shall not be disclosed to any third party, except as follows:

> \(a\) as required by applicable federal, state, or local law, rule, regulation, or legal process, including without limitation a subpoena, court order, or regulatory inquiry, provided that the disclosing Party shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide the other Party with prompt written notice of such requirement prior to disclosure, and shall cooperate with the other Party\'s reasonable efforts to obtain a protective order or other appropriate remedy to limit the scope of such disclosure;
>
> \(b\) to the Parties\' respective legal counsel, auditors, tax advisors, accountants, and insurance carriers, in each case who have a bona fide need to know the terms of this Agreement in connection with the performance of their professional duties, and who shall be bound by obligations of confidentiality no less restrictive than those contained in this Article 6;
>
> \(c\) by Nexford, to Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Partners, LP (as Nexford\'s parent entity and private equity sponsor) and to Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Management LLC (as the management company of Nexford\'s sponsor), and to Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A. (as Nexford\'s senior secured lender), in each case to the extent such disclosure is required under Nexford\'s governing documents, limited partnership agreement, operating agreement, or credit agreements, including without limitation Section 6.03(b) of the Credit Agreement dated March 12, 2021, by and among Nexford, as borrower, and Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A., as administrative agent and lender;
>
> \(d\) by Nexford, to its external auditors, Hargrove Kellner CPAs LLP, to the extent reasonably necessary for the preparation of Nexford\'s financial statements, tax returns, or other financial reporting obligations;
>
> \(e\) by Cardinal Peak, to its members, managers, and financial advisors, to the extent reasonably necessary for internal governance, financial planning, and reporting purposes;
>
> \(f\) as required in connection with any federal, state, or local tax filing or audit by either Party; and
>
> \(g\) in connection with any action or proceeding brought to enforce the terms of this Agreement.

**6.2 No Public Statements.** Neither Party shall make, authorize, or cause to be made any public statement, press release, social media posting, or other public disclosure regarding the Surcharge Dispute, the Litigation, the mediation proceedings, or the existence, terms, or conditions of this Agreement, without the prior written consent of the other Party, which consent may be withheld in such Party\'s sole discretion. In the event that either Party receives an inquiry from any media outlet, trade publication, or other third party regarding the Surcharge Dispute or the Litigation, the receiving Party shall respond only that \"the matter has been resolved\" and shall make no further comment without the prior written consent of the other Party, except as required by applicable law.

**6.3 Remedies for Breach.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that a breach or threatened breach of this Article 6 may cause irreparable harm to the non-breaching Party for which monetary damages alone would be an insufficient and inadequate remedy. Accordingly, each Party shall be entitled to seek equitable relief, including injunctive relief and specific performance, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity, without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting a bond or other security.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

**7.1 Representations of Nexford.** Nexford hereby represents and warrants to Cardinal Peak, as of the Effective Date, as follows:

> \(a\) **Organization and Good Standing.** Nexford is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware and has all requisite corporate power and authority to own, lease, and operate its properties and to carry on its business as presently conducted.
>
> \(b\) **Authorization.** The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by Nexford have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate action, including any required approvals of Nexford\'s board of directors, and no further corporate proceedings on the part of Nexford are necessary to authorize this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby.
>
> \(c\) **Enforceability.** This Agreement constitutes a valid and binding obligation of Nexford, enforceable against Nexford in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity.
>
> \(d\) **Financial Capacity.** Nexford has the financial capacity and access to sufficient funds to pay the Settlement Amount in full in accordance with the payment schedule set forth in Section 2.2, and knows of no reason why it would be unable to make such payments when due.
>
> \(e\) **No Assignment of Claims.** Nexford has not assigned, transferred, conveyed, pledged, or otherwise encumbered any of the claims released by Nexford herein to any third party, and no third party has any interest, legal or equitable, in any such claims.

**7.2 Representations of Cardinal Peak.** Cardinal Peak hereby represents and warrants to Nexford, as of the Effective Date, as follows:

> \(a\) **Organization and Good Standing.** Cardinal Peak is a limited liability company duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Colorado and has all requisite limited liability company power and authority to own, lease, and operate its properties and to carry on its business as presently conducted.
>
> \(b\) **Authorization.** The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by Cardinal Peak have been duly authorized by all necessary action of its members and managers, including any required approvals under Cardinal Peak\'s operating agreement, and no further proceedings on the part of Cardinal Peak are necessary to authorize this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby.
>
> \(c\) **Enforceability.** This Agreement constitutes a valid and binding obligation of Cardinal Peak, enforceable against Cardinal Peak in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity.
>
> \(d\) **No Assignment of Claims.** Cardinal Peak has not assigned, transferred, conveyed, pledged, or otherwise encumbered any of the claims released by Cardinal Peak herein to any third party, and no third party has any interest, legal or equitable, in any such claims.

**7.3 Mutual Representations.** Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party, as of the Effective Date, as follows:

> \(a\) **Understanding and Voluntariness.** It has read this Agreement in its entirety, understands all of its terms and conditions, and voluntarily executes this Agreement without duress, coercion, or undue influence.
>
> \(b\) **Legal Counsel.** It has been represented by competent legal counsel of its own choosing in connection with the negotiation, drafting, and execution of this Agreement. Nexford has been represented by Calderwood & Harkness LLP, Chicago, Illinois. Cardinal Peak has been represented by Blackwood Stein & Associates LLP, Denver, Colorado.
>
> \(c\) **Opportunity to Investigate.** It has had a full and fair opportunity to investigate and evaluate the facts, law, claims, defenses, and arguments relating to the Surcharge Dispute and the Litigation, and has relied upon its own judgment and the advice of its counsel in entering into this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE 8 --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**8.1 Mutual Indemnification.** Each Party (the \"**Indemnifying Party**\") shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other Party and its respective Released Parties (each, an \"**Indemnified Party**\") from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, judgments, settlements, costs, and expenses (including without limitation reasonable attorneys\' fees, expert witness fees, and costs of investigation) arising out of or relating to any breach by the Indemnifying Party of any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation contained in this Agreement. The obligation of indemnification set forth in this Section 8.1 shall survive the execution of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby. The Indemnified Party shall provide prompt written notice to the Indemnifying Party of any claim for which indemnification is sought; provided, however, that any delay in providing such notice shall not relieve the Indemnifying Party of its indemnification obligations except to the extent the Indemnifying Party is materially prejudiced by such delay.

**[ARTICLE 9 --- MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**9.1 Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and interpreted in accordance with, the internal laws of the State of Illinois, without giving effect to any choice-of-law or conflict-of-laws rules or provisions (whether of the State of Illinois or any other jurisdiction) that would cause the application of the laws of any jurisdiction other than the State of Illinois.

**9.3 Entire Agreement.** This Agreement, together with the Mutual Termination Agreement to be executed pursuant to Article 5, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, understandings, negotiations, discussions, representations, and commitments, whether oral or written, between the Parties relating to the subject matter hereof, including without limitation the Term Sheet dated August 2, 2023. **9.4 Amendments.** This Agreement may not be amended, modified, restated, or supplemented in any respect except by a written instrument duly executed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No oral modification or amendment of this Agreement shall be of any force or effect.

**9.5 Waiver.** The failure of either Party to enforce any provision of this Agreement at any time or for any period of time shall not constitute a waiver of that Party\'s right to enforce that provision or any other provision of this Agreement at any future time. Any purported assignment in violation of this Section 9.7 shall be null and void.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
**(e)** **\"Direct Contribution\"** means the sum of Four Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$4,500,000.00) to be paid by GPR and GPCP, jointly and severally, as part of the Settlement Amount, as more particularly described in Section 2.2(b) of this Agreement.
**(h)** **\"Escrow Agreement\"** means the Escrow Agreement of even date herewith, entered into among RGC, GPR, GPCP, and the Escrow Agent, establishing the terms and conditions governing the escrow account into which the Settlement Amount shall be deposited and from which the Settlement Amount shall be disbursed.
**(o)** **\"Settlement Amount\"** means the aggregate sum of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,750,000.00) to be paid to RGC in full and final settlement of the Action and the Released Claims, as more particularly described in Article 2 of this Agreement.
**Section 2.1 --- Settlement Amount.**
In consideration of the mutual releases, covenants, and agreements set forth in this Agreement, Defendants shall cause the payment of the aggregate sum of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,750,000.00) to RGC (the \"Settlement Amount\"). The Settlement Amount represents the total and complete monetary consideration to be paid in connection with the settlement of the Action and the Released Claims, and no additional monetary payments shall be owed by Defendants or any other person or entity to RGC in connection with this settlement.
The Settlement Amount shall be funded from the following two sources:
Within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date (i.e., on or before February 5, 2025), all components of the Settlement Amount shall be deposited into the escrow account established at Great Basin Trust Company, N.A. pursuant to the Escrow Agreement. Specifically:
Upon confirmation by the Escrow Agent that the full Settlement Amount of \$14,750,000.00 has been deposited into the escrow account, and subject to the terms and conditions of the Escrow Agreement, the Escrow Agent shall disburse the Settlement Amount to RGC (or as directed by RGC in written wire transfer instructions) within five (5) business days of such confirmation. RGC shall provide the Escrow Agent with complete and accurate wire transfer instructions in advance of disbursement. The Parties agree that no disbursement shall be made until the Escrow Agent has confirmed receipt of the full Settlement Amount, and partial disbursements shall not be permitted absent the prior written agreement of all Parties and the Escrow Agent.
In the event that any portion of the Settlement Amount is not deposited into the escrow account within the time period prescribed in Section 2.3, interest shall accrue at the rate of ten percent (10%) per annum (the legal rate under California law, as set forth in California Civil Code Section 3289) on the unpaid balance from the applicable due date until the date on which such amount is actually deposited in full.
In the event of a material default in payment --- defined as the failure to deposit any portion of the Settlement Amount within fifteen (15) business days after written notice from RGC to Defendants specifying the deficiency --- RGC shall have the right, at its sole election, to pursue either of the following remedies:
Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own federal, state, local, and foreign tax obligations, if any, arising from the payment, receipt, or disbursement of the Settlement Amount. Defendants and Ironclad shall not be responsible for any tax obligations of RGC arising from the receipt of the Settlement Amount, and RGC shall indemnify and hold harmless Defendants and Ironclad from and against any and all tax liabilities, penalties, interest, or other amounts assessed against Defendants or Ironclad as a result of RGC\'s failure to report or pay its tax obligations with respect to the Settlement Amount.
RGC acknowledges that it has been advised to consult with independent tax counsel regarding the federal, state, local, and foreign tax treatment of the Settlement Amount, and that none of the Defendants, Ironclad, or their respective counsel has made or is making any representation or warranty regarding the tax treatment or tax consequences of any payment made or received pursuant to this Agreement. The Escrow Agent shall issue any applicable tax reporting forms (including, without limitation, IRS Form 1099) in accordance with applicable law, and the Parties shall provide the Escrow Agent with any taxpayer identification forms (including, without limitation, IRS Form W-9) reasonably requested by the Escrow Agent.
Effective upon confirmation by the Escrow Agent that the full Settlement Amount of \$14,750,000.00 has been deposited into the escrow account established pursuant to the Escrow Agreement, RGC, on behalf of itself and each of its past, present, and future officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, successors, assigns, affiliates, subsidiaries (including, without limitation, Redstone Digital and Crimson Studios), parent entities, and all persons and entities acting on its behalf or claiming through it (collectively, the \"RGC Releasors\"), hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, acquits, and forever discharges each of the Defendants and their respective past, present, and future officers, directors, members, partners, managers, employees, agents, representatives, heirs, executors, administrators, successors, assigns, insurers (including, without limitation, Ironclad Surety & Insurance Co.), and affiliates (collectively, the \"Defendant Releasees\") from any and all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, demands, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, specialties, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, promises, variances, trespasses, damages, judgments, extents, executions, liabilities, losses, costs, expenses, attorneys\' fees, and any and all obligations of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, asserted or unasserted, foreseen or unforeseen, matured or unmatured, accrued or unaccrued, liquidated or unliquidated, contingent or non-contingent, that any RGC Releasor now has, has ever had, or may hereafter have against any Defendant Releasee, arising out of, relating to, or in any way connected with the Reports, the Action, the subject matter of the Action, or any of the facts, events, transactions, occurrences, acts, omissions, representations, statements, or publications alleged, described, or referenced in the Action or the Reports (collectively, the \"Released Claims\").
> **(a)** The specific dollar amount of the Settlement Amount (\$14,750,000.00);
> **(b)** The allocation of the Settlement Amount between the Insurance Contribution (\$10,250,000.00) and the Direct Contribution (\$4,500,000.00);
> **(c)** The specific financial details of Defendants\' contribution to the Settlement Amount, including the sources and amounts of funding, the identity of Defendants\' insurer and the terms of coverage, and any other financial or economic terms of the settlement that are not otherwise publicly disclosed through court filings; and
Defendants represent and warrant to RGC that Ironclad Surety & Insurance Co. has reviewed and approved the terms of this settlement, and that Ironclad has agreed, subject to the terms and conditions of directors-and-officers / media-liability Policy No. ML-2023-07714, to fund the Insurance Contribution in the amount of Ten Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$10,250,000.00) as part of the Settlement Amount. Defendants further represent that the Insurance Contribution does not exceed the remaining available limits under Policy No. ML-2023-07714 and that no other claims, settlements, or payments have been made or are pending under such policy that would impair or reduce the available limits below the amount of the Insurance Contribution.
In the event Ironclad fails or refuses to fund the Insurance Contribution within the time period prescribed in Section 2.3, Defendants shall promptly notify RGC in writing and shall use reasonable best efforts to cause Ironclad to comply with its obligations. Nothing in this Agreement shall relieve Defendants of their obligation to cause the full Settlement Amount to be deposited into escrow within the prescribed time period; Defendants\' obligations under Article 2 are not conditioned upon or excused by any delay or failure by Ironclad.
No Party may assign, transfer, delegate, or otherwise dispose of its rights or obligations under this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the prior written consent of each other Party, and any purported assignment, transfer, or delegation in violation of this Section 11.8 shall be null and void and of no force or effect; provided, however, that RGC may assign its right to receive the Settlement Amount (or any portion thereof) to a successor-in-interest in connection with a merger, consolidation, acquisition, or reorganization involving RGC, without the consent of the other Parties, so long as the assignee assumes RGC\'s obligations under this Agreement in writing.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
**(e) Election.** The Husband hereby elects to retain the Marital Residence and to buy out the Wife\'s 35% share of the net equity. The buyout amount of \$2.555 million is included within the lump sum cash payment set forth in Section 4.2 of this Agreement.
**Section 4.2 --- Lump Sum Cash Payment.**
**(a) Total Amount.** The Husband shall pay to the Wife a total lump sum cash payment of **\$14.5 million**, which includes the buyout of the Wife\'s 35% share of the net equity of the Marital Residence in the amount of \$2.555 million, as set forth in Section 3.5(d)--(e) above.
**(b) Payment Schedule.** The lump sum cash payment shall be made in two (2) installments as follows:
The Husband shall pay to the Wife an additional cash sum of **\$3.15 million**, payable concurrently with the first lump sum installment due under Section 4.2(b)(i) of this Agreement. This additional cash payment covers miscellaneous marital personal property, furnishings, household items, and other agreed items not otherwise specifically addressed in this Agreement. Upon receipt of this payment, the Wife shall have no further claim to any marital personal property, furnishings, or household items in the Husband\'s possession.
  Lump sum cash payment (Section 4.2), inclusive of Marital Residence buyout (\$2.555M)   \$14,500,000
Note: The Marital Residence buyout of \$2.555 million is a component of the \$14.5 million lump sum cash payment and is not separately additive. The Wife also retains her own retirement accounts (SEP-IRA and 401(k)) valued at \$1.1 million. The total distribution figure of \$31.2 million represents the Parties\' agreed global resolution inclusive of Wife\'s retained Separate Property.
**Section 5.1 --- Amount and Duration.** The Husband shall pay to the Wife spousal maintenance in the amount of **Fifteen Thousand Dollars (\$15,000) per month** for a period of **forty-eight (48) months**, commencing on the first day of the first full calendar month following the entry of the Judgment of Divorce. The total spousal maintenance obligation of the Husband under this Agreement is \$720,000 (\$15,000 × 48 months). This amount is consistent with the cap set forth in the Prenuptial Agreement, which provides that for marriages lasting ten (10) or more years, spousal maintenance shall not exceed \$15,000 per month for a period not to exceed five (5) years. The Parties have agreed to a four (4)-year term as part of this global settlement.
**Section 7.1 --- Basic Child Support.** The Husband shall pay to the Wife child support in the amount of **\$8,500 per month per child**, for a total of **\$17,000 per month** for both Children combined. Payments shall commence on the first day of the first full calendar month following the entry of the Judgment of Divorce. This child support obligation supersedes and replaces the temporary (pendente lite) child support order of \$14,000 per month entered by the Court on September 30, 2022. The Parties acknowledge that the child support amount set forth herein has been calculated by reference to the factors set forth in DRL § 240(1-b) and reflects the Parties\' agreement as to the appropriate level of support for the Children in light of the Husband\'s income, the Wife\'s income, and the Children\'s needs.
**Section 7.2 --- Duration.** The Husband\'s obligation to pay child support for each child shall continue until the earlier of: (a) the child\'s attainment of the age of eighteen (18); or (b) the child\'s graduation from high school, whichever occurs later, unless the child is sooner emancipated by marriage, entry into the military, or other legally recognized event constituting emancipation under New York law. In the event that a child becomes emancipated, the Husband\'s child support obligation for that child shall terminate effective as of the date of emancipation, and the monthly payment shall be reduced to \$8,500 per month for the remaining child.
**(a)** As security for the payment of the second installment of \$6.5 million due under Section 4.2(b)(ii), the Husband shall, within thirty (30) days of the execution of this Agreement, deposit the sum of \$6.5 million into an escrow account at Trident National Bank, to be held by an independent escrow agent mutually agreed upon by the Parties. The escrow funds shall be invested in short-term U.S. Treasury obligations or money market instruments, and all interest earned shall accrue to the benefit of the Husband. The escrow funds shall be released to the Wife upon the occurrence of the payment due date (i.e., within twelve months of the Judgment of Divorce), or earlier at the Husband\'s election.
**Section 14.3 --- Joint Debts.** Any joint credit obligations, joint credit card accounts, or other joint debts existing as of the Effective Date shall be the sole responsibility of the Husband. The Husband shall pay off and close all joint credit accounts within sixty (60) days of the entry of the Judgment of Divorce. The Husband shall indemnify, defend, and hold the Wife harmless from and against any and all claims, demands, judgments, or actions by any creditor in connection with any joint obligation, and this indemnification obligation shall survive the entry of the Judgment of Divorce.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
**1.12 \"Settlement Amount\"** means One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$1,620,000.00), as further described in Section 2.1 of this Agreement.
**2.1 Amount.** In full and complete settlement of all Claims arising during the Release Period, Defendant shall pay Plaintiffs and their counsel a total Settlement Amount of One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$1,620,000.00), allocated as follows:
For the avoidance of doubt, the total back-royalty component of the Settlement Amount is One Million Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$1,425,000.00), consisting of the FDL Payment (\$712,500.00) and the Mariposa Payment (\$712,500.00). The total Settlement Amount is One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$1,620,000.00), consisting of the back-royalty component (\$1,425,000.00) plus the Fee Payment (\$195,000.00).
**2.2 Payment Schedule.** The Settlement Amount shall be paid in two (2) installments as follows:
> \(a\) **First Installment.** One Million One Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$1,100,000.00), due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date, no later than September 13, 2023 (the \"First Payment Date\"). The First Installment shall be allocated pro rata among the FDL Payment, the Mariposa Payment, and the Fee Payment based on each payment\'s proportion of the total Settlement Amount. Specifically, of the First Installment:
**3.3 Royalty Rate.** During the License Term, Defendant shall pay Plaintiffs a royalty of three and one-half cents (\$0.035) per individual stream of each Work through the Crescendo Stream platform (each such individual playback event constituting a \"stream\" for purposes of royalty calculation). The per-stream royalty shall apply regardless of whether the stream is initiated by an end user, generated through an algorithm or automated playlist, or played as part of a sublicensed content package under Section 3.6. Royalties due under this Section 3.3 shall be allocated equally between FDL Publishing (with respect to the underlying musical compositions) and Mariposa Sound (with respect to the underlying sound recordings).
**3.4 Minimum Annual Guarantee.** Notwithstanding the per-stream royalty rate set forth in Section 3.3, Defendant shall pay Plaintiffs a minimum annual guarantee (the \"MAG\") of One Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$175,000.00) for each License Year during the License Term. The total MAG over the full License Term shall be Five Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$525,000.00) (\$175,000.00 multiplied by three (3) License Years). The MAG shall operate as follows:
> \(b\) If the aggregate per-stream royalties earned by Plaintiffs in a given License Year are less than the MAG for that License Year, Defendant shall pay to Plaintiffs the difference between the MAG and the actual per-stream royalties earned within thirty (30) days after the end of such License Year. Such payment is sometimes referred to herein as the \"MAG Shortfall Payment.\"
**3.5 Reporting and Payment.** Defendant shall provide Plaintiffs with a detailed written royalty statement within thirty (30) days after the end of each calendar quarter during the License Term (i.e., within thirty (30) days after September 30, December 31, March 31, and June 30 of each year, with the first reporting period running from the Effective Date through September 30, 2023). Each royalty statement shall set forth, at a minimum: (i) the title and identifying information of each Work streamed during the applicable quarter; (ii) the total number of streams of each Work during the applicable quarter; (iii) the per-stream royalty rate; (iv) the aggregate royalty amount due for each Work; (v) the total royalty amount due for the quarter; and (vi) a cumulative year-to-date total of streams and royalties for the applicable License Year. Payment of all quarterly royalties shall accompany each royalty statement. All royalty statements and corresponding payments shall be sent simultaneously to Plaintiffs and to Thornfield Music Administration, Inc. (as Plaintiffs\' designated catalog administrator), 6363 Wilshire Boulevard, Suite 410, Los Angeles, California 90048, Attention: Raymond O. Sato, President.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged by each Party, the Parties agree as follows:
**1.1 Payment Amount and Schedule.** As settlement consideration for the claims asserted by Fonseca against the Rennick Parties, Rennick shall pay, or cause to be paid, to Fonseca the aggregate sum of Nine Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$975,000) (the \"Settlement Amount\"), payable in two installments as follows:
**1.2 Late Payment.** In the event that any installment of the Settlement Amount is not received by Fonseca on or before its applicable Installment Due Date, the unpaid amount shall bear interest at the rate of ten percent (10%) per annum, calculated on a simple interest basis from the applicable Installment Due Date through and including the date of actual receipt of such payment by Fonseca. The accrual of interest under this Section 1.2 shall not limit or waive any other rights or remedies available to Fonseca under this Agreement, at law, or in equity, including the right to seek enforcement of this Agreement pursuant to California Code of Civil Procedure Section 664.6 as contemplated by Section 7.1 hereof.
**1.3 Source of Funds.** The Settlement Amount shall be the personal obligation of Rennick individually and shall not be paid, directly or indirectly, from the funds, accounts, assets, or revenues of CMP. Rennick represents and warrants that he has sufficient personal financial resources and liquidity to satisfy the Settlement Amount in accordance with the payment schedule set forth in Section 1.1 above. Nothing in this Section 1.3 shall prohibit Rennick from using funds distributed to him by CMP in the ordinary course of business in accordance with the Partnership Agreement and the Restated Waterfall (as defined below), provided that no CMP distribution shall be accelerated, preferentially directed, or otherwise manipulated for the purpose of funding the Settlement Amount.
> **(c)** The payment by Rennick of the Settlement Amount in accordance with Section 1 of this Agreement shall constitute full and complete satisfaction, settlement, and resolution of any and all claims, demands, causes of action, and liabilities that Fonseca or CMP may have against Rennick, RSV, or any of their respective affiliates, arising from, relating to, or in connection with the Excess Fees, including without limitation claims for breach of the Partnership Agreement, breach of fiduciary duty, unjust enrichment, conversion, accounting, constructive trust, disgorgement, or any other legal or equitable theory.
> **(d)** Upon Fonseca\'s receipt of the Settlement Amount in full, no further clawback, restitution, repayment, refund, offset, credit, or other remedy of any kind shall be required of or available against Rennick, RSV, or any of their respective affiliates with respect to the Excess Fees. For the avoidance of doubt, this Section 3 does not release or waive any rights of Fonseca with respect to management fees paid or payable by CMP on or after January 1, 2023, which shall be governed exclusively by the Restated Waterfall an pay such invoices within thirty (30) days of receipt.
\(d\) Each Party shall pay its respective share of the Compliance Monitor\'s fees and expenses directly to the Compliance Monitor on a quarterly basis, within thirty (30) days of receipt of each quarterly invoice. In the event the actual fees and expenses exceed the estimated amounts, the Parties shall bear such excess in the same sixty percent (60%) / forty percent (40%) allocation, provided that any single-quarter invoice exceeding the pro rata quarterly estimate by more than fifteen percent (15%) shall require advance written approval from counsel for both Cascade and Verdana.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
**Section 1.6 --- \"Settlement Amount.\"** \"Settlement Amount\" means Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars and No Cents (\$14,750,000.00).
**Section 2.1 --- Payment Amount.** In consideration of the mutual covenants, releases, and agreements set forth in this Agreement, Cascade shall pay to Vantor the Settlement Amount of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars and No Cents (\$14,750,000.00) in full and final satisfaction of all Released Claims. **Section 2.2 --- Payment Method and Timing.** The Settlement Amount shall be paid by Cascade to Vantor by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States Dollars to a bank account designated by Vantor in writing. In consideration of the mutual releases, covenants, and agreements set forth in this Agreement, Defendants shall cause the payment of the aggregate sum of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,750,000.00) to RGC (the \"Settlement Amount\"). **1.12 \"Settlement Amount\"** means One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$1,620,000.00), as further described in Section 2.1 of this Agreement.

**1.1 Payment Amount and Schedule.** As settlement consideration for the claims asserted by Fonseca against the Rennick Parties, Rennick shall pay, or cause to be paid, to Fonseca the aggregate sum of Nine Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$975,000) (the \"Settlement Amount\"), payable in two installments as follows:

**4.1 Restoration to Distributable Profit Pool.** The Parties acknowledge that the aggregate sum of Eight Hundred Forty-Seven Thousand Two Hundred Dollars (\$847,200) in domestic distribution revenues received by CMP was reclassified on CMP\'s books and records as recoupable advance repayments. The Parties agree that such reclassification was not authorized under the Partnership Agreement and that the reclassified amounts shall be restored to CMP\'s distributable profit pool, with such restoration treated as retroactive to the fiscal quarters in which the revenues were originally received by CMP, as follows:
**(j) \"Settlement Payment\"** means Four Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$4,200,000).

**(a)** Within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date, Palomar shall pay to Quorum the Settlement Payment in the amount of Four Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$4,200,000). Payment shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to a bank account designated by Quorum in writing in accordance with the wire transfer instructions to be provided pursuant to Section 2.1(b) below.

**(c)** If the Settlement Payment is not received in full by Quorum within the thirty (30) day period specified in Section 2.1(a), interest shall accrue on the unpaid amount at the rate of the lesser of eighteen percent (18%) per annum or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, calculated from the date the Settlement Payment was due until the date the Settlement Payment is received in full by Quorum.

The Parties acknowledge and agree that the total effective value of the settlement consideration provided for under Sections 2.1 and 2.2 of this Agreement is Six Million One Hundred Fifty-Six Thousand Dollars (\$6,156,000), comprised of the Settlement Payment in the amount of Four Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$4,200,000) and the aggregate fee reduction in the amount of One Million Nine Hundred Fifty-Six Thousand Dollars (\$1,956,000). The Parties further acknowledge that this settlement consideration represents a compromise and does not reflect any determination as to the merits or value of any Claims released hereunder.

Except as specifically provided in this Agreement, the indemnification cap set forth in Section 12.2 of the MSA, which provides for a maximum aggregate liability of two times (2×) the trailing twelve-month fees paid (currently equal to Thirty-Two Million Six Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$32,600,000)), shall remain in full force and effect and shall not be deemed waived, modified, reduced, exhausted, or otherwise affected by the settlement consideration paid or provided under this Agreement. 41: **A. Franchise Relationship.** Verimark operates and franchises approximately 340 branded hotel properties across the southeastern United States under the \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand\" flags. For fiscal year 2021, Verimark reported consolidated revenue of approximately \$1.42 billion, of which the franchise segment contributed approximately \$218 million. Coastal Palms is the operator of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties --- eighteen (18) operating under the Verimark Suites flag and four (4) operating under the Verimark Select flag --- located across the States of Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. The first Franchise License Agreement (\"FLA\") between Verimark and Coastal Palms was executed on June 15, 2007, for a Verimark Suites property located in Naples, Florida. Over the following years, Coastal Palms and its affiliates executed a total of twenty-two (22) individual FLAs with Verimark, the most recent of which was dated September 3, 2019. Each FLA provides for a twenty (20)-year initial term and is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any disputes in Broward County, Florida. Under each FLA, Coastal Palms is required to pay the following fees: (i) a royalty equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") (FLA § 4.1); (ii) a marketing-fund contribution equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR (FLA § 4.2); and (iii) a technology fee of twelve dollars and fifty cents (\$12.50) per available room per month, adjusted annually for changes in the Consumer Price Index, with such adjustment capped at three percent (3%) per year (FLA § 4.3). Late-payment interest under the FLAs accrues at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly (FLA § 4.6). Additionally, FLA § 15.3 provides for liquidated damages upon termination for cause in an amount equal to three times (3×) the trailing-twelve-month royalties per property... (line truncated to 2000 chars)
