43: **B. The Litigation.** On November 8, 2021, a former Coastal Palms regional controller, Janet Kerrigan, reported to Verimark\'s compliance hotline allegations of systematic revenue underreporting by the Coastal Palms Parties. In response, Verimark retained Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP to conduct a franchise-compliance audit of the Coastal Palms properties. Thornbury\'s preliminary findings, delivered to Verimark on January 18, 2022, indicated that the audited properties had underreported GRR by approximately twenty-six percent (26%) for the period spanning fiscal years 2019 through 2021. Verimark issued a Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms on February 4, 2022, demanding that Coastal Palms cure the identified breaches within thirty (30) days in accordance with FLA § 14.1. Coastal Palms, through its counsel Whitfield, Barrow & Crane LLP, responded by letter dated February 28, 2022, denying any material breach and contesting the methodology and conclusions of the Thornbury audit. No cure was tendered by Coastal Palms within the thirty (30)-day period, which expired on March 6, 2022. On March 7, 2022, Verimark filed a ten-count Complaint in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, bearing Case Number 1021-00006 (the \"Litigation\"), asserting claims for: (i) breach of contract --- royalties; (ii) breach of contract --- marketing fund; (iii) breach of contract --- technology fees; (iv) breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing; (v) fraudulent concealment; (vi) negligent misrepresentation; (vii) unjust enrichment; (viii) declaratory judgment; (ix) accounting; and (x) civil conspiracy. In the Complaint, Verimark claimed damages in the approximate aggregate amount of \$150,000,000, consisting of: (a) \$16,095,000 in direct underpayments of royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees; (b) \$28,400,000 in contractual late-payment interest calculated in accordance with FLA § 4.6; a... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

45: **C. Summary Judgment Ruling.** On February 9, 2024, the Court (the Honorable Richard M. Calloway, Circuit Judge) entered an Order granting Verimark\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on Count I (Breach of Contract --- Royalties) and Count II (Breach of Contract --- Marketing Fund), finding as a matter of law that Coastal Palms\' exclusion of revenues collected by Suncoast Room Management Inc. from its calculation and reporting of GRR constituted a material breach of FLA §§ 4.1 and 4.2. The Court denied Coastal Palms\' Cross-Motion for Summary Judgment on all counts and deferred the determination of damages to trial.
46: 
47: **D. Mediation and Settlement.** On February 23, 2024, the Parties agreed to submit their dispute to mediation before the Honorable Patricia Everwood (Retired), of Everwood Dispute Resolution PLLC. A two-day mediation session was conducted on March 14 and 15, 2024, at 396 Alhambra Circle, Suite 800, Coral Gables, Florida 33134. A tentative settlement was reached on the second day of mediation, March 15, 2024, and the Parties executed a written term sheet memorializing the principal terms of the settlement on March 22, 2024. The Parties now desire to fully and finally resolve all claims and counterclaims in the Litigation, and all related disputes among the Parties, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.
48: 
49: **E. Desire to Settle.** The Parties acknowledge the uncertainty, risk, and expense inherent in continued litigation and trial, and each Party has made an independent assessment of the merits and risks of its respective claims and defenses. The Parties desire to avoid the further burden and expense of trial and to resolve their disputes amicably and in full. Entry into this Agreement is not, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or the validity of any claim or defense by any Party. Each Party has been represented by competent legal counsel of its choosing in the negotiation and execution of this Agreement, and each Party has had a full and fair opportunity to review, analyze, and negotiate the terms set forth herein.
50:

105: **1.25** \"**Verimark Brands**\" means \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand,\" together with all associated trademarks, service marks, logos, trade dress, proprietary systems (including reservation systems, property management systems, and revenue management systems), and all other intellectual property owned, licensed, or controlled by Verimark in connection with the branding and operation of its franchised hotel properties.
106: 
107: **[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**
108: 
109: **Section 2.1 --- Total Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, causes of action, and disputes among the Parties, whether asserted or unasserted, known or unknown, arising from or relating to the Existing FLAs, the Litigation, or the subject matter thereof, the Coastal Palms Parties shall pay to Verimark a total Settlement Amount of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable as follows:
110: 
111: > \(a\) The Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), payable at the Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 below; and
112: >
113: > \(b\) The Structured Payments totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in eight (8) semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, in accordance with Section 2.3 below.
114: 
115: The Payment Schedule setting forth the dates, amounts, and interest calculations for all payments under this Article II is attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference.
116: 
117: **Section 2.2 --- Initial Payment.** On the Closing Date, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) by wire transfer of immediately available funds from the escrow account established at Ironclad National Bank for the purposes of this settlement to Verimark\'s designated account. Verimark shall provide Coastal Palms with complete wire-transfer instructions for the designated receiving account no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. Upon receipt of the Initial Payment, Verimark\'s counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, at 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, shall promptly issue a written confirmation of receipt to counsel for the Coastal Palms Parties. The obligation to make the Initial Payment is unconditional and shall not be subject to any right of setoff, counterclaim, defense, or deduction.
118: 
119: **Section 2.3 --- Structured Payments.** Following the payment of the Initial Payment, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the remaining Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000) in eight (8) equal semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, on the following schedule:
120: 
121: > \(a\) The first installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2024.
122: >
123: > \(b\) The second installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2025.
124: >
125: > \(c\) The third installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2025.
126: >
127: > \(d\) The fourth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2026.
128: >
129: > \(e\) The fifth installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2026.
130: >
131: > \(f\) The sixth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2027.
132: >
133: > \(g\) The seventh installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2027.
134: >
135: > \(h\) The eighth and final installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2028.
136: 
137: All Structured Payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Verimark in accordance with the wire-transfer instructions provided pursuant to Section 2.2, or to such other account as Verimark may designate in writing from time to time upon not less than ten (10) business days\' prior notice to Coastal Palms.
138: 
139: **Section 2.4 --- Interest on Structured Payments.** Interest shall accrue on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments at a rate of six and one-half percent (6.5%) per annum, simple interest, calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed. Interest shall begin to accrue on the Closing Date and shall be calculated on the then-outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments. Interest payments shall be due and payable concurrently with each semi-annual installment payment. The amount of interest due with each installment shall be calculated by multiplying the outstanding principal balance as of the first day of the applicable interest period by the annual interest rate of 6.5%, and then multiplying the result by a fraction, the numerator of which is the actual number of days elapsed during such interest period and the denominator of which is 365. A detailed schedule setting forth the estimated interest amounts due with each installment is set forth in Exhibit A.
140: 
141: **Section 2.5 --- Late Payments.** Any Structured Payment (including any concurrent interest payment) not received by Verimark within ten (10) business days of its scheduled due date shall bear additional default interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month on the overdue amount, calculated from the original due date until the date on which such overdue amount is received by Verimark in full. This default interest shall be in addition to, and not in substitution for, the interest otherwise payable under Section 2.4. If Coastal Palms fails to cure a late payment within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the overdue payment and the amount due, such failure shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 2.7 of this Agreement. Nothing in this Section 2.5 shall be construed to extend the due date for any Structured Payment or to waive Verimark\'s right to declare an Event of Default following the expiration of the applicable cure period.
142: 
143: **Section 2.6 --- Prepayment.** Coastal Palms may, at its option, prepay all or any portion of the Structured Payments at any time without premium, penalty, or additional charge of any kind. Any partial prepayment shall be applied first to any accrued and unpaid interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, and second to the scheduled installments in inverse order of maturity (i.e., applied first to the most distant scheduled installment, then to the next most distant, and so on), thereby reducing the total interest obligation over the remaining term. Coastal Palms shall provide Verimark with not less than five (5) business days\' prior written notice of any prepayment, specifying the amount and intended date of such prepayment. Verimark shall recalculate the interest amounts due on any remaining installments following any partial prepayment and shall provide an updated Payment Schedule to Coastal Palms within ten (10) business days of receipt of any such prepayment.
144: 
145: **Section 2.7 --- Events of Default and Acceleration.** An \"Event of Default\" shall be deemed to have occurred upon the happening of any of the following:
146: 
147: > \(a\) **Payment Default.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to make any payment of the Structured Payments, accrued interest, or any other monetary obligation under this Agreement within thirty (30) days of the date on which Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such payment default;
148: >
149: > \(b\) **Covenant Default.** Breach by any Coastal Palms Party of any material covenant, agreement, or obligation under this Agreement (other than a payment obligation, which is governed by clause (a) above) that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such breach in reasonable detail;
150: >
151: > \(c\) **Bankruptcy or Insolvency.** The commencement of any voluntary or involuntary proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code, Title 11, United States Code, or under any state insolvency, receivership, dissolution, or similar statute, by or against any Coastal Palms Party, or the appointment of a receiver, trustee, custodian, or similar official for the business, assets, or property of any Coastal Palms Party, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors by any Coastal Palms Party;
152: >
153: > \(d\) **Breach of Representations and Warranties.** Any representation or warranty made by any Coastal Palms Party in this Agreement or in any ancillary document delivered in connection herewith that is materially inaccurate, false, or misleading as of the date on which it was made, and such inaccuracy, falsity, or misleading character is not cured within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the same;
154: >
155: > \(e\) **De-Identification Failure.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to comply with the de-identification requirements set forth in Article VII of this Agreement by the De-Identification Deadline.
156: 
157: Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Verimark may, at its sole election and upon written notice to Coastal Palms, declare the entire outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon and all other amounts owing under this Agreement, immediately due and payable in full, without further notice, demand, presentment, or protest, all of which are hereby waived by the Coastal Palms Parties. Acceleration of the Structured Payments pursuant to this Section 2.7 shall not constitute a waiver of, or limit, any other rights or remedies available to Verimark at law or in equity, including, without limitation, the right to enforce the Security Agreement, to seek collection under the Personal Guaranties, to pursue foreclosure on the Collateral Properties, and to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from the Court.
158: 
159: **Section 2.8 --- Tax Treatment.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of all federal, state, and local taxes, and for the filing of all tax returns and reports, arising from or attributable to the payments received or made by such Party under this Agreement. The Parties agree that, for federal and state income-tax purposes, the Settlement Amount shall be treated by all Parties as compensatory damages and that no portion of the Settlement Amount shall be characterized as punitive damages, penalties, or interest for tax purposes, except to the extent required by applicable law. The Coastal Palms Parties shall be solely responsible for any and all withholding obligations, including but not limited to any obligation to withhold and remit taxes on behalf of Verimark, if any such obligation exists under applicable law. No Party shall take any position on any tax return or in any proceeding before any taxing authority that is inconsistent with the treatment described in this Section 2.8, unless required to do so by a final determination (as defined in Section 1313(a) of the Internal Revenue Code) of a court of competent jurisdiction or an applicable taxing authority.
160: 
161: **[ARTICLE III --- SECURITY FOR STRUCTURED PAYMENTS]{.underline}**
162: 
163: **Section 3.1 --- Security Interest.** To secure the prompt and full payment and performance of all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, including, without limitation, the payment of all Structured Payments, accrued interest thereon, default interest, and any indemnification obligations arising under Article X, Coastal Palms hereby grants to Verimark a first-priority security interest in the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties identified in Schedule 3.1 attached hereto (the \"Collateral Properties\"), together with all improvements, fixtures, furnishings, equipment, accounts, general intangibles, and proceeds related thereto (collectively, the \"Collateral\"). The aggregate appraised value of the Collateral Properties, as determined by independent appraisals conducted by licensed commercial real-estate appraisers within the ninety (90)-day period preceding the Closing Date, is not less than Seventy-One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$71,200,000). The security interest granted hereunder shall be evidenced by the Security Agreement, which shall be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F and shall be executed and delivered concurrently with the execution of this Agreement.

The UCC-1 Financing Statement shall identify the following:

167: > **Debtor:** Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108
168: >
169: > **Secured Party:** Verimark Hospitality Group Inc., 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301
170: 
171: Coastal Palms shall execute and deliver all additional documents, instruments, and agreements, including without limitation continuation statements, amendments, and such other filings and recordings, as may be reasonably necessary or requested by Verimark from time to time to perfect, preserve, and maintain the first-priority status of Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. Coastal Palms shall bear all costs and expenses associated with such filings.
172: 
173: **Section 3.3 --- Personal Guaranties.** Concurrently with the execution of this Agreement, R. Brecker and Prescott shall each execute and deliver to Verimark a Personal Guaranty, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, pursuant to which R. Brecker and Prescott shall jointly and severally, absolutely, unconditionally, and irrevocably guarantee the full and prompt payment and performance of all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, including, without limitation, all Structured Payments, accrued interest, default interest, indemnification obligations, and any and all other amounts that may become due and owing under this Agreement. The Personal Guaranties shall remain in full force and effect until all Structured Payments, accrued interest, and all other obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement have been paid or performed in full to the complete satisfaction of Verimark.

The Parties further acknowledge that the eight (8) Collateral Properties identified in Schedule 3.1, which secure Verimark\'s security interest under this Agreement, are unencumbered by any mortgage, lien, or security interest held by Ironclad. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed or interpreted so as to impair, subordinate, modify, or otherwise affect in any manner whatsoever the existing liens, security interests, or other rights of Ironclad under its mortgage-loan agreements with the Coastal Palms Parties. Coastal Palms represents and warrants that it has provided written notice to Ironclad of the existence and terms of this Agreement and the grant of the security interest to Verimark, and that Ironclad has not objected to the transactions contemplated hereby. Ironclad is an intended third-party beneficiary of this Section 3.4 and of Section 9.5 of this Agreement.
176: 
177: **Section 3.5 --- Release of Security Interest.** Upon the payment in full of all Structured Payments, accrued interest, default interest (if any), and all other obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, Verimark shall, within thirty (30) days of such payment in full: (a) file UCC-3 Termination Statements with the Florida Secured Transaction Registry and all other applicable filing offices; and (b) execute and deliver to Coastal Palms such releases, satisfactions, and other documents and instruments as may be reasonably necessary to evidence the termination and release of Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. Verimark shall bear its own costs associated with the preparation and filing of such termination statements and releases.

**SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE**
This **SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE** (this \"Agreement\") is entered into and made effective as of April 22, 2024 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among the following parties:

**VERIMARK HOSPITALITY GROUP INC.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal place of business at 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, and whose common stock is listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"VHMK\" (hereinafter referred to as \"Verimark\" or \"VHG\");
and

**COASTAL PALMS FRANCHISE HOLDINGS LLC**, a Florida limited liability company, with its principal office at 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108 (hereinafter referred to as \"Coastal Palms\" or \"CPFH\");

**RANDALL \"RANDY\" BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who serves as the Managing Member and holds a sixty percent (60%) equity interest in Coastal Palms, and who also serves as the President of Suncoast Room Management Inc. (hereinafter referred to as \"R. Brecker\");
**THERESA BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a fifteen percent (15%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"T. Brecker\");

**NOLAN PRESCOTT**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a twenty-five percent (25%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"Prescott\");
**GULF BREEZE HOSPITALITY LLC**, a Florida limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Gulf Breeze\");
**SAVANNAH LODGING PARTNERS LLC**, a Georgia limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Savannah Lodging\");
**SUNCOAST ROOM MANAGEMENT INC.**, a Florida corporation (hereinafter referred to as \"Suncoast\");

Coastal Palms, R. Brecker, T. Brecker, Prescott, Gulf Breeze, Savannah Lodging, and Suncoast are collectively referred to herein as the \"Coastal Palms Parties.\" Verimark and the Coastal Palms Parties are collectively referred to herein as the \"Parties\" and each individually as a \"Party.\"
**[RECITALS]{.underline}**
**WHEREAS:**

**A. Franchise Relationship.** Verimark operates and franchises approximately 340 branded hotel properties across the southeastern United States under the \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand\" flags. For fiscal year 2021, Verimark reported consolidated revenue of approximately \$1.42 billion, of which the franchise segment contributed approximately \$218 million. Coastal Palms is the operator of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties --- eighteen (18) operating under the Verimark Suites flag and four (4) operating under the Verimark Select flag --- located across the States of Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. The first Franchise License Agreement (\"FLA\") between Verimark and Coastal Palms was executed on June 15, 2007, for a Verimark Suites property located in Naples, Florida. Over the following years, Coastal Palms and its affiliates executed a total of twenty-two (22) individual FLAs with Verimark, the most recent of which was dated September 3, 2019. Each FLA provides for a twenty (20)-year initial term and is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any disputes in Broward County, Florida. Under each FLA, Coastal Palms is required to pay the following fees: (i) a royalty equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") (FLA § 4.1); (ii) a marketing-fund contribution equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR (FLA § 4.2); and (iii) a technology fee of twelve dollars and fifty cents (\$12.50) per available room per month, adjusted annually for changes in the Consumer Price Index, with such adjustment capped at three percent (3%) per year (FLA § 4.3). Late-payment interest under the FLAs accrues at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly (FLA § 4.6). Additionally, FLA § 15.3 provides for liquidated damages upon termination for cause in an amount equal to three times (3×) the trailing-twelve-month royalties per property... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

**B. The Litigation.** On November 8, 2021, a former Coastal Palms regional controller, Janet Kerrigan, reported to Verimark\'s compliance hotline allegations of systematic revenue underreporting by the Coastal Palms Parties. In response, Verimark retained Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP to conduct a franchise-compliance audit of the Coastal Palms properties. Thornbury\'s preliminary findings, delivered to Verimark on January 18, 2022, indicated that the audited properties had underreported GRR by approximately twenty-six percent (26%) for the period spanning fiscal years 2019 through 2021. Verimark issued a Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms on February 4, 2022, demanding that Coastal Palms cure the identified breaches within thirty (30) days in accordance with FLA § 14.1. Coastal Palms, through its counsel Whitfield, Barrow & Crane LLP, responded by letter dated February 28, 2022, denying any material breach and contesting the methodology and conclusions of the Thornbury audit. No cure was tendered by Coastal Palms within the thirty (30)-day period, which expired on March 6, 2022. On March 7, 2022, Verimark filed a ten-count Complaint in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, bearing Case Number 1021-00006 (the \"Litigation\"), asserting claims for: (i) breach of contract --- royalties; (ii) breach of contract --- marketing fund; (iii) breach of contract --- technology fees; (iv) breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing; (v) fraudulent concealment; (vi) negligent misrepresentation; (vii) unjust enrichment; (viii) declaratory judgment; (ix) accounting; and (x) civil conspiracy. In the Complaint, Verimark claimed damages in the approximate aggregate amount of \$150,000,000, consisting of: (a) \$16,095,000 in direct underpayments of royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees; (b) \$28,400,000 in contractual late-payment interest calculated in accordance with FLA § 4.6; a... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

**C. Summary Judgment Ruling.** On February 9, 2024, the Court (the Honorable Richard M. Calloway, Circuit Judge) entered an Order granting Verimark\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on Count I (Breach of Contract --- Royalties) and Count II (Breach of Contract --- Marketing Fund), finding as a matter of law that Coastal Palms\' exclusion of revenues collected by Suncoast Room Management Inc. from its calculation and reporting of GRR constituted a material breach of FLA §§ 4.1 and 4.2. The Court denied Coastal Palms\' Cross-Motion for Summary Judgment on all counts and deferred the determination of damages to trial.

**D. Mediation and Settlement.** On February 23, 2024, the Parties agreed to submit their dispute to mediation before the Honorable Patricia Everwood (Retired), of Everwood Dispute Resolution PLLC. A two-day mediation session was conducted on March 14 and 15, 2024, at 396 Alhambra Circle, Suite 800, Coral Gables, Florida 33134. A tentative settlement was reached on the second day of mediation, March 15, 2024, and the Parties executed a written term sheet memorializing the principal terms of the settlement on March 22, 2024. The Parties now desire to fully and finally resolve all claims and counterclaims in the Litigation, and all related disputes among the Parties, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.

**E. Desire to Settle.** The Parties acknowledge the uncertainty, risk, and expense inherent in continued litigation and trial, and each Party has made an independent assessment of the merits and risks of its respective claims and defenses. The Parties desire to avoid the further burden and expense of trial and to resolve their disputes amicably and in full. Entry into this Agreement is not, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or the validity of any claim or defense by any Party. Each Party has been represented by competent legal counsel of its choosing in the negotiation and execution of this Agreement, and each Party has had a full and fair opportunity to review, analyze, and negotiate the terms set forth herein.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, releases, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**1.23** \"**Structured Payments**\" means the eight (8) semi-annual payments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in accordance with Section 2.3 of this Agreement, the first such payment being due on October 22, 2024, and the last such payment being due on April 22, 2028, as more fully described in the Payment Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit A.

**[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Total Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, causes of action, and disputes among the Parties, whether asserted or unasserted, known or unknown, arising from or relating to the Existing FLAs, the Litigation, or the subject matter thereof, the Coastal Palms Parties shall pay to Verimark a total Settlement Amount of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable as follows:
> \(a\) The Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), payable at the Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 below; and

> \(b\) The Structured Payments totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in eight (8) semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, in accordance with Section 2.3 below.
The Payment Schedule setting forth the dates, amounts, and interest calculations for all payments under this Article II is attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference.

**Section 2.2 --- Initial Payment.** On the Closing Date, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) by wire transfer of immediately available funds from the escrow account established at Ironclad National Bank for the purposes of this settlement to Verimark\'s designated account. Verimark shall provide Coastal Palms with complete wire-transfer instructions for the designated receiving account no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. Upon receipt of the Initial Payment, Verimark\'s counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, at 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, shall promptly issue a written confirmation of receipt to counsel for the Coastal Palms Parties. The obligation to make the Initial Payment is unconditional and shall not be subject to any right of setoff, counterclaim, defense, or deduction.

**Section 2.3 --- Structured Payments.** Following the payment of the Initial Payment, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the remaining Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000) in eight (8) equal semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, on the following schedule:
> \(a\) The first installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2024.
> \(b\) The second installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2025.
> \(c\) The third installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2025.
> \(d\) The fourth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2026.
> \(e\) The fifth installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2026.
> \(f\) The sixth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2027.
> \(g\) The seventh installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2027.
> \(h\) The eighth and final installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2028.

All Structured Payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Verimark in accordance with the wire-transfer instructions provided pursuant to Section 2.2, or to such other account as Verimark may designate in writing from time to time upon not less than ten (10) business days\' prior notice to Coastal Palms.

**Section 2.4 --- Interest on Structured Payments.** Interest shall accrue on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments at a rate of six and one-half percent (6.5%) per annum, simple interest, calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed. Interest shall begin to accrue on the Closing Date and shall be calculated on the then-outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments. Interest payments shall be due and payable concurrently with each semi-annual installment payment. The amount of interest due with each installment shall be calculated by multiplying the outstanding principal balance as of the first day of the applicable interest period by the annual interest rate of 6.5%, and then multiplying the result by a fraction, the numerator of which is the actual number of days elapsed during such interest period and the denominator of which is 365. A detailed schedule setting forth the estimated interest amounts due with each installment is set forth in Exhibit A.

**Section 2.5 --- Late Payments.** Any Structured Payment (including any concurrent interest payment) not received by Verimark within ten (10) business days of its scheduled due date shall bear additional default interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month on the overdue amount, calculated from the original due date until the date on which such overdue amount is received by Verimark in full. This default interest shall be in addition to, and not in substitution for, the interest otherwise payable under Section 2.4. If Coastal Palms fails to cure a late payment within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the overdue payment and the amount due, such failure shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 2.7 of this Agreement. Nothing in this Section 2.5 shall be construed to extend the due date for any Structured Payment or to waive Verimark\'s right to declare an Event of Default following the expiration of the applicable cure period.

**Section 2.6 --- Prepayment.** Coastal Palms may, at its option, prepay all or any portion of the Structured Payments at any time without premium, penalty, or additional charge of any kind. Any partial prepayment shall be applied first to any accrued and unpaid interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, and second to the scheduled installments in inverse order of maturity (i.e., applied first to the most distant scheduled installment, then to the next most distant, and so on), thereby reducing the total interest obligation over the remaining term. Coastal Palms shall provide Verimark with not less than five (5) business days\' prior written notice of any prepayment, specifying the amount and intended date of such prepayment. Verimark shall recalculate the interest amounts due on any remaining installments following any partial prepayment and shall provide an updated Payment Schedule to Coastal Palms within ten (10) business days of receipt of any such prepayment.
**Section 2.7 --- Events of Default and Acceleration.** An \"Event of Default\" shall be deemed to have occurred upon the happening of any of the following:

> \(a\) **Payment Default.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to make any payment of the Structured Payments, accrued interest, or any other monetary obligation under this Agreement within thirty (30) days of the date on which Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such payment default;

> \(b\) **Covenant Default.** Breach by any Coastal Palms Party of any material covenant, agreement, or obligation under this Agreement (other than a payment obligation, which is governed by clause (a) above) that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such breach in reasonable detail;

> \(c\) **Bankruptcy or Insolvency.** The commencement of any voluntary or involuntary proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code, Title 11, United States Code, or under any state insolvency, receivership, dissolution, or similar statute, by or against any Coastal Palms Party, or the appointment of a receiver, trustee, custodian, or similar official for the business, assets, or property of any Coastal Palms Party, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors by any Coastal Palms Party;

> \(d\) **Breach of Representations and Warranties.** Any representation or warranty made by any Coastal Palms Party in this Agreement or in any ancillary document delivered in connection herewith that is materially inaccurate, false, or misleading as of the date on which it was made, and such inaccuracy, falsity, or misleading character is not cured within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the same;

> \(e\) **De-Identification Failure.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to comply with the de-identification requirements set forth in Article VII of this Agreement by the De-Identification Deadline.

Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Verimark may, at its sole election and upon written notice to Coastal Palms, declare the entire outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon and all other amounts owing under this Agreement, immediately due and payable in full, without further notice, demand, presentment, or protest, all of which are hereby waived by the Coastal Palms Parties. Acceleration of the Structured Payments pursuant to this Section 2.7 shall not constitute a waiver of, or limit, any other rights or remedies available to Verimark at law or in equity, including, without limitation, the right to enforce the Security Agreement, to seek collection under the Personal Guaranties, to pursue foreclosure on the Collateral Properties, and to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from the Court.

**Section 2.8 --- Tax Treatment.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of all federal, state, and local taxes, and for the filing of all tax returns and reports, arising from or attributable to the payments received or made by such Party under this Agreement. The Parties agree that, for federal and state income-tax purposes, the Settlement Amount shall be treated by all Parties as compensatory damages and that no portion of the Settlement Amount shall be characterized as punitive damages, penalties, or interest for tax purposes, except to the extent required by applicable law. The Coastal Palms Parties shall be solely responsible for any and all withholding obligations, including but not limited to any obligation to withhold and remit taxes on behalf of Verimark, if any such obligation exists under applicable law. No Party shall take any position on any tax return or in any proceeding before any taxing authority that is inconsistent with the treatment described in this Section 2.8, unless required to do so by a final determination (as defined in Section 1313(a) of the Internal Revenue Code) of a court of competent jurisdiction or an applicable taxing authority.
**[ARTICLE III --- SECURITY FOR STRUCTURED PAYMENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Security Interest.** To secure the prompt and full payment and performance of all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, including, without limitation, the payment of all Structured Payments, accrued interest thereon, default interest, and any indemnification obligations arising under Article X, Coastal Palms hereby grants to Verimark a first-priority security interest in the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties identified in Schedule 3.1 attached hereto (the \"Collateral Properties\"), together with all improvements, fixtures, furnishings, equipment, accounts, general intangibles, and proceeds related thereto (collectively, the \"Collateral\"). The aggregate appraised value of the Collateral Properties, as determined by independent appraisals conducted by licensed commercial real-estate appraisers within the ninety (90)-day period preceding the Closing Date, is not less than Seventy-One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$71,200,000). The security interest granted hereunder shall be evidenced by the Security Agreement, which shall be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F and shall be executed and delivered concurrently with the execution of this Agreement.

**Section 3.2 --- UCC Filings.** To perfect the security interest granted under Section 3.1, Coastal Palms hereby authorizes Verimark, and Verimark\'s counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, to prepare, execute, and file on behalf of Coastal Palms UCC-1 Financing Statements with the Florida Secured Transaction Registry and with any other filing office in any jurisdiction where filing may be necessary or advisable to perfect or maintain Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. The UCC-1 Financing Statement shall identify the following:
> **Debtor:** Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108
> **Secured Party:** Verimark Hospitality Group Inc., 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301

Coastal Palms shall execute and deliver all additional documents, instruments, and agreements, including without limitation continuation statements, amendments, and such other filings and recordings, as may be reasonably necessary or requested by Verimark from time to time to perfect, preserve, and maintain the first-priority status of Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. Coastal Palms shall bear all costs and expenses associated with such filings.

**Section 3.3 --- Personal Guaranties.** Concurrently with the execution of this Agreement, R. Brecker and Prescott shall each execute and deliver to Verimark a Personal Guaranty, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, pursuant to which R. Brecker and Prescott shall jointly and severally, absolutely, unconditionally, and irrevocably guarantee the full and prompt payment and performance of all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, including, without limitation, all Structured Payments, accrued interest, default interest, indemnification obligations, and any and all other amounts that may become due and owing under this Agreement. The Personal Guaranties shall remain in full force and effect until all Structured Payments, accrued interest, and all other obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement have been paid or performed in full to the complete satisfaction of Verimark.

**Section 3.4 --- Relationship with Ironclad National Bank.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that Ironclad National Bank (\"Ironclad\") holds first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) Properties, with an aggregate outstanding principal balance of approximately Ninety-Four Million Dollars (\$94,000,000) as of the date hereof. The Parties further acknowledge that the eight (8) Collateral Properties identified in Schedule 3.1, which secure Verimark\'s security interest under this Agreement, are unencumbered by any mortgage, lien, or security interest held by Ironclad. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed or interpreted so as to impair, subordinate, modify, or otherwise affect in any manner whatsoever the existing liens, security interests, or other rights of Ironclad under its mortgage-loan agreements with the Coastal Palms Parties. Coastal Palms represents and warrants that it has provided written notice to Ironclad of the existence and terms of this Agreement and the grant of the security interest to Verimark, and that Ironclad has not objected to the transactions contemplated hereby. Ironclad is an intended third-party beneficiary of this Section 3.4 and of Section 9.5 of this Agreement.

**Section 3.5 --- Release of Security Interest.** Upon the payment in full of all Structured Payments, accrued interest, default interest (if any), and all other obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, Verimark shall, within thirty (30) days of such payment in full: (a) file UCC-3 Termination Statements with the Florida Secured Transaction Registry and all other applicable filing offices; and (b) execute and deliver to Coastal Palms such releases, satisfactions, and other documents and instruments as may be reasonably necessary to evidence the termination and release of Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. Verimark shall bear its own costs associated with the preparation and filing of such termination statements and releases.

Secured Obligations.** The obligations secured by this Security Agreement (the \"Secured Obligations\") include: (a) all Structured Payments in the aggregate amount of \$62,500,000; (b) all accrued interest thereon at the rate of 6.5% per annum, simple interest; (c) all default interest that may accrue under Section 2.5 of the Settlement Agreement; (d) all indemnification obligations of Debtor under Article X of the Settlement Agreement; and (e) all other amounts, obligations, and liabilities of Debtor to Secured Party under the Settlement Agreement, whether now existing or hereafter arising.

> \(d\) **Taxes and Assessments.** Debtor shall pay all taxes, assessments, charges, and levies imposed upon the Collateral or upon Debtor by reason of its ownership of the Collateral, before such taxes or assessments become delinquent;

> \(e\) **Further Assurances.** Debtor shall execute and deliver such additional documents and instruments as Secured Party may reasonably request to evidence, perfect, or maintain the security interest created hereby.

Remedies.** Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Secured Party may exercise all rights and remedies available to a secured party under the Florida Uniform Commercial Code (Chapter 679, Florida Statutes), under other applicable law, and under this Security Agreement, including, without limitation:
> \(a\) Declare all Secured Obligations immediately due and payable;
> \(b\) Take possession of the Collateral;
> \(c\) Foreclose on the Collateral Properties in accordance with applicable law;
> \(d\) Sell, lease, or otherwise dispose of the Collateral at public or private sale;
> \(e\) Collect and apply all rents, profits, and revenues from the Collateral to the Secured Obligations; and
> \(f\) Exercise any other rights or remedies available at law or in equity.
All rights and remedies of Secured Party under this Security Agreement are cumulative and not exclusive of any other rights or remedies.

Termination.** Upon the payment and performance in full of all Secured Obligations, the security interest created hereby shall terminate and be of no further force or effect, and Secured Party shall file UCC-3 Termination Statements and execute and deliver such releases and satisfactions as are required under Section 3.5 of the Settlement Agreement.

1: **[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**
2: 
3: **Effective Date: December 19, 2023**
4: 
5: This Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (this \"Agreement\") is entered into as of December 19, 2023 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among the following parties:
6: 
7: **VERIMARK HOSPITALITY GROUP INC.**, a Delaware corporation (\"VHG\" or \"Plaintiff\"), with its principal offices at 1900 Brickell Avenue, Suite 3200, Miami, Florida 33129;
8: 
9: **IRONCLAD INDEMNITY CORPORATION**, a Connecticut-domiciled stock insurance company (\"Ironclad\"), with its principal offices at 55 Constitution Boulevard, Hartford, Connecticut 06103;
10: 
11: **PINNACLE SURPLUS LINES INC.**, a Texas-domiciled surplus-lines insurer (\"Pinnacle\"), with its principal offices at 200 Congress Avenue, Suite 1400, Austin, Texas 78701;
12: 
13: **MONTCLAIR ASSURANCE COMPANY**, a New York-domiciled admitted insurance carrier (\"Montclair\"), with its principal offices at 1 Liberty Plaza, 38th Floor, New York, New York 10006; and
14: 
15: **SOVEREIGN RE LTD.**, a Bermuda-domiciled excess carrier (\"Sovereign Re\"), with its principal offices at 14 Front Street, Hamilton HM 11, Bermuda.
16: 
17: VHG, Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re are referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"
18: 
19: Right-click to update Table of Contents
20: 
21: **[RECITALS]{.underline}**
22: 
23: **WHEREAS:**
24: 
25: **A.** VHG is a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, whose common stock is publicly traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"VMRK,\" and which maintains its principal executive offices at 1900 Brickell Avenue, Suite 3200, Miami, Florida 33129. VHG is engaged in the business of owning, operating, and managing luxury resort hotel properties in the State of Florida. As of the Effective Date, VHG\'s portfolio of properties includes, among others, the following three resort hotel properties (collectively, the \"Insured Properties\"):
26: 
27: > \(i\) the Verimark Grand Key Resort, located at Mile Marker 48, Marathon, Florida 33050, a 287-room full-service luxury resort and marina situated in the Florida Keys;
28: >
29: > \(ii\) the Verimark Harborview Hotel & Conference Center, located at 1400 Estero Boulevard, Fort Myers Beach, Florida 33931, a 412-room beachfront hotel and conference center situated on the Gulf Coast of Florida; and
30: >
31: > \(iii\) the Verimark Sunset Shores, located at 7200 Gulf Boulevard, St. Pete Beach, Florida 33706, a 194-room boutique luxury hotel and spa situated on the barrier island of St. Pete Beach on the Gulf of Mexico.
32: 
33: **B.** In connection with VHG\'s ownership and operation of the Insured Properties, VHG procured and maintained a layered insurance program consisting of property and business-interruption coverage as follows:
34: 
35: > \(i\) Ironclad is a stock insurance company domiciled in the State of Connecticut and licensed to transact insurance business in the State of Florida. Ironclad issued to VHG an all-risk property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number IIC-PRP-2022-07541, for the policy period commencing July 1, 2022 and ending July 1, 2023, providing primary coverage with a per-occurrence limit of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) for property damage and business-interruption losses, subject to a deductible of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per occurrence (the \"Primary Policy\").
36: >
37: > \(ii\) Pinnacle is a surplus-lines insurer domiciled in the State of Texas and authorized to transact surplus-lines insurance business in the State of Florida. Pinnacle issued to VHG a first excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number PSL-XS1-2022-3390, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Fifteen Million Dollars (\$15,000,000) in coverage in excess of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the Primary Policy (the \"First Excess Policy\").
38: >
39: > \(iii\) Montclair is an admitted insurance carrier domiciled in the State of New York and licensed to transact insurance business in the State of Florida. Montclair issued to VHG a second excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number MAC-XS2-2022-09817, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) in coverage in excess of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the combined limits of the Primary Policy and the First Excess Policy (the \"Second Excess Policy\").
40: >
41: > \(iv\) Sovereign Re is an excess carrier domiciled in Bermuda and authorized to transact excess insurance business relating to risks situated in the State of Florida. Sovereign Re issued to VHG a third excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number SRL-XS3-2022-5102, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) in coverage in excess of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the combined limits of the Primary Policy, the First Excess Policy, and the Second Excess Policy (the \"Third Excess Policy\").
42: 
43: The Primary Policy, the First Excess Policy, the Second Excess Policy, and the Third Excess Policy are referred to herein collectively as the \"Policies.\" The Policies provide aggregate tower limits of Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) above the Five Hundred Thousand Dollar (\$500,000) deductible applicable under the Primary Policy.
44: 
45: **C.** On September 18, 2022, Hurricane Callista, classified by the National Hurricane Center as a Category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Veltason Hurricane Wind Scale, made landfall in the Lower Florida Keys with maximum sustained winds of approximately 145 miles per hour and produced storm surge inundation of approximately eight (8) to fourteen (14) feet above normal tide levels in Monroe County and approximately six (6) to ten (10) feet above normal tide levels in Lee County. Hurricane Callista caused catastrophic and widespread damage throughout southern Florida, including significant damage to coastal structures, resort properties, marinas, and critical infrastructure along the Florida Keys and the Gulf Coast of southwestern Florida. As a direct and proximate result of Hurricane Callista, the Insured Properties sustained catastrophic property damage and experienced prolonged and severe business interruption, including complete closure of the Grand Key Resort and the Harborview Hotel & Conference Center for extended periods, and partial closure of Sunset Shores (collectively, the \"Hurricane Callista Losses\"). VHG submitted an initial notice of loss to Ironclad, as primary carrier, on September 22, 2022, four days following the landfall of Hurricane Callista. Thereafter, VHG submitted a sworn statement in proof of loss to Ironclad on November 15, 2022, pursuant to the requirements of the Primary Policy, asserting total business-interruption losses of approximately Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) across the Insured Properties.
46: 
47: **D.** On October 12, 2022, Ironclad, through its designated third-party claims administrator, Arbor Claims Services LLC, and its coverage counsel, Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP, issued a reservation of rights letter to VHG with respect to VHG\'s claim for business-interruption losses. On February 3, 2023, Ironclad issued a formal denial of coverage for VHG\'s business-interruption claim, asserting, among other grounds, that: (i) the Primary Policy contained a named-windstorm sub-limit that capped business-interruption recovery at an amount substantially below VHG\'s claimed losses; (ii) the period of restoration was subject to dispute, and VHG had failed to establish the proper period of restoration for business-interruption coverage; (iii) certain claimed losses were attributable to flood and storm surge, which were subject to a concurrent causation analysis and the flood exclusion in the Primary Policy; and (iv) VHG had failed to adequately mitigate its losses in breach of its duties under the Primary Policy. On February 10, 2023, Pinnacle, through its coverage counsel, Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP, followed Ironclad\'s denial on a follow-form basis and denied coverage for VHG\'s business-interruption claim to the extent it fell within Pinnacle\'s layer. Montclair and Sovereign Re, through their joint coverage counsel, Delvecchio & Kraus LLP, did not issue formal denials of coverage but reserved all rights under their respective policies, asserting that their excess layers would not be reached based on the application of the named-windstorm sub-limit asserted by Ironclad and Pinnacle.
48: 
49: **E.** On March 1, 2023, VHG filed a multi-count complaint in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, in and for Miami-Dade County, captioned *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corp., Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc., Montclair Assurance Company, and Sovereign Re Ltd.*, Case No. 2022-CA-031547, assigned to the Honorable Catherine Embry, Circuit Judge (the \"Litigation\"). In the Litigation, VHG asserted claims for: (i) breach of contract against all four Insurer Parties; (ii) declaratory judgment seeking a judicial determination of coverage rights under the Policies; and (iii) bad faith, including both statutory bad faith under Section 624.155 of the Florida Statutes and common-law bad faith, against all four Insurer Parties. VHG\'s complaint alleged total business-interruption losses of approximately Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000), comprised of approximately Thirty-One Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$31,400,000) attributable to the Verimark Grand Key Resort, approximately Eighteen Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$18,700,000) attributable to the Verimark Harborview Hotel & Conference Center, and approximately Nine Million Nine Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$9,900,000) attributable to the Verimark Sunset Shores. On April 15, 2023, Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re, through their respective counsel, filed answers and affirmative defenses denying liability and raising numerous defenses to VHG\'s claims. Thereafter, the Parties conducted extensive fact discovery, including the exchange of voluminous documents, written discovery, and depositions of party representatives, including depositions of VHG\'s Chief Executive Officer Marcus Ellsworth, VHG\'s Chief Financial Officer Diane Calder, VHG\'s General Counsel Nathaniel Driscoll, Ironclad\'s Senior Vice President of Claims Victor Haddon, and Arbor Claims Services LLC\'s lead adjuster Denise Whitford. The Parties also conducted expert discovery, including the retention a... (line truncated to 2000 chars)
50: 
51: **F.** On December 4 and December 5, 2023, the Parties participated in a two-day mediation session before the Honorable Richard Mendelson (Ret.) of Keystone Dispute Resolution Inc. in Miami, Florida. All Parties appeared through their respective counsel and authorized corporate representatives with full settlement authority. At the conclusion of the mediation on December 5, 2023, the Parties reached an agreement in principle to resolve all disputes and claims among them, which agreement in principle was memorialized in a binding term sheet executed by all Parties on that date. The Parties subsequently negotiated the terms of this Agreement to memorialize the final and comprehensive terms of their settlement.
52: 
53: **G.** The Parties desire to fully and finally resolve any and all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, disputes, and controversies between and among them arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies, without any admission of liability, fault, or wrongdoing by any Party, and on the terms and conditions set forth herein.
54: 
55: **NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
56: 
57: **[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**
58: 
59: **Section 1.1** *Defined Terms.* As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article I shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.
60: 
61: > \(a\) \"Agreement\" means this Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, together with all Exhibits attached hereto, as the same may be amended or modified from time to time in accordance with Section 9.4.
62: >
63: > \(b\) \"Claim\" or \"Claims\" means any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, expenses (including, without limitation, attorneys\' fees and costs of litigation), obligations, judgments, liens, debts, and rights of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, asserted or unasserted, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, accrued or not yet accrued, liquidated or unliquidated, arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies.
64: >
65: > \(c\) \"Effective Date\" means the date on which this Agreement is fully executed by all Parties, which the Parties agree is December 19, 2023.
66: >
67: > \(d\) \"Hurricane Callista Losses\" means any and all property damage, business-interruption losses, loss of rents, extra expenses, debris removal costs, increased cost of construction, loss of business income, and all related losses, costs, and expenses sustained or incurred by VHG at or in connection with the Insured Properties arising out of or relating to Hurricane Callista, which made landfall on September 18, 2022, and the aftermath thereof.
68: >
69: > \(e\) \"Insured Properties\" has the meaning set forth in Recital A of this Agreement.
70: >
71: > \(f\) \"Insurer Parties\" means Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re, together with their respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, underwriters, reinsurers, predecessors, successors, and assigns.
72: >

**Effective Date: December 19, 2023**
This Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (this \"Agreement\") is entered into as of December 19, 2023 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among the following parties:
**VERIMARK HOSPITALITY GROUP INC.**, a Delaware corporation (\"VHG\" or \"Plaintiff\"), with its principal offices at 1900 Brickell Avenue, Suite 3200, Miami, Florida 33129;
**IRONCLAD INDEMNITY CORPORATION**, a Connecticut-domiciled stock insurance company (\"Ironclad\"), with its principal offices at 55 Constitution Boulevard, Hartford, Connecticut 06103;
**PINNACLE SURPLUS LINES INC.**, a Texas-domiciled surplus-lines insurer (\"Pinnacle\"), with its principal offices at 200 Congress Avenue, Suite 1400, Austin, Texas 78701;
**MONTCLAIR ASSURANCE COMPANY**, a New York-domiciled admitted insurance carrier (\"Montclair\"), with its principal offices at 1 Liberty Plaza, 38th Floor, New York, New York 10006; and
**SOVEREIGN RE LTD.**, a Bermuda-domiciled excess carrier (\"Sovereign Re\"), with its principal offices at 14 Front Street, Hamilton HM 11, Bermuda.
VHG, Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re are referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**
**WHEREAS:**

**A.** VHG is a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, whose common stock is publicly traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"VMRK,\" and which maintains its principal executive offices at 1900 Brickell Avenue, Suite 3200, Miami, Florida 33129. VHG is engaged in the business of owning, operating, and managing luxury resort hotel properties in the State of Florida. As of the Effective Date, VHG\'s portfolio of properties includes, among others, the following three resort hotel properties (collectively, the \"Insured Properties\"):
> \(i\) the Verimark Grand Key Resort, located at Mile Marker 48, Marathon, Florida 33050, a 287-room full-service luxury resort and marina situated in the Florida Keys;

> \(ii\) the Verimark Harborview Hotel & Conference Center, located at 1400 Estero Boulevard, Fort Myers Beach, Florida 33931, a 412-room beachfront hotel and conference center situated on the Gulf Coast of Florida; and

> \(iii\) the Verimark Sunset Shores, located at 7200 Gulf Boulevard, St. Pete Beach, Florida 33706, a 194-room boutique luxury hotel and spa situated on the barrier island of St. Pete Beach on the Gulf of Mexico.

**B.** In connection with VHG\'s ownership and operation of the Insured Properties, VHG procured and maintained a layered insurance program consisting of property and business-interruption coverage as follows:

> \(i\) Ironclad is a stock insurance company domiciled in the State of Connecticut and licensed to transact insurance business in the State of Florida. Ironclad issued to VHG an all-risk property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number IIC-PRP-2022-07541, for the policy period commencing July 1, 2022 and ending July 1, 2023, providing primary coverage with a per-occurrence limit of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) for property damage and business-interruption losses, subject to a deductible of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per occurrence (the \"Primary Policy\").

> \(ii\) Pinnacle is a surplus-lines insurer domiciled in the State of Texas and authorized to transact surplus-lines insurance business in the State of Florida. Pinnacle issued to VHG a first excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number PSL-XS1-2022-3390, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Fifteen Million Dollars (\$15,000,000) in coverage in excess of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the Primary Policy (the \"First Excess Policy\").

> \(iii\) Montclair is an admitted insurance carrier domiciled in the State of New York and licensed to transact insurance business in the State of Florida. Montclair issued to VHG a second excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number MAC-XS2-2022-09817, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) in coverage in excess of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the combined limits of the Primary Policy and the First Excess Policy (the \"Second Excess Policy\").

> \(iv\) Sovereign Re is an excess carrier domiciled in Bermuda and authorized to transact excess insurance business relating to risks situated in the State of Florida. Sovereign Re issued to VHG a third excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number SRL-XS3-2022-5102, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) in coverage in excess of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the combined limits of the Primary Policy, the First Excess Policy, and the Second Excess Policy (the \"Third Excess Policy\").

The Primary Policy, the First Excess Policy, the Second Excess Policy, and the Third Excess Policy are referred to herein collectively as the \"Policies.\" The Policies provide aggregate tower limits of Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) above the Five Hundred Thousand Dollar (\$500,000) deductible applicable under the Primary Policy.

**C.** On September 18, 2022, Hurricane Callista, classified by the National Hurricane Center as a Category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Veltason Hurricane Wind Scale, made landfall in the Lower Florida Keys with maximum sustained winds of approximately 145 miles per hour and produced storm surge inundation of approximately eight (8) to fourteen (14) feet above normal tide levels in Monroe County and approximately six (6) to ten (10) feet above normal tide levels in Lee County. Hurricane Callista caused catastrophic and widespread damage throughout southern Florida, including significant damage to coastal structures, resort properties, marinas, and critical infrastructure along the Florida Keys and the Gulf Coast of southwestern Florida. As a direct and proximate result of Hurricane Callista, the Insured Properties sustained catastrophic property damage and experienced prolonged and severe business interruption, including complete closure of the Grand Key Resort and the Harborview Hotel & Conference Center for extended periods, and partial closure of Sunset Shores (collectively, the \"Hurricane Callista Losses\"). VHG submitted an initial notice of loss to Ironclad, as primary carrier, on September 22, 2022, four days following the landfall of Hurricane Callista. Thereafter, VHG submitted a sworn statement in proof of loss to Ironclad on November 15, 2022, pursuant to the requirements of the Primary Policy, asserting total business-interruption losses of approximately Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) across the Insured Properties.

**D.** On October 12, 2022, Ironclad, through its designated third-party claims administrator, Arbor Claims Services LLC, and its coverage counsel, Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP, issued a reservation of rights letter to VHG with respect to VHG\'s claim for business-interruption losses. On February 3, 2023, Ironclad issued a formal denial of coverage for VHG\'s business-interruption claim, asserting, among other grounds, that: (i) the Primary Policy contained a named-windstorm sub-limit that capped business-interruption recovery at an amount substantially below VHG\'s claimed losses; (ii) the period of restoration was subject to dispute, and VHG had failed to establish the proper period of restoration for business-interruption coverage; (iii) certain claimed losses were attributable to flood and storm surge, which were subject to a concurrent causation analysis and the flood exclusion in the Primary Policy; and (iv) VHG had failed to adequately mitigate its losses in breach of its duties under the Primary Policy. On February 10, 2023, Pinnacle, through its coverage counsel, Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP, followed Ironclad\'s denial on a follow-form basis and denied coverage for VHG\'s business-interruption claim to the extent it fell within Pinnacle\'s layer. Montclair and Sovereign Re, through their joint coverage counsel, Delvecchio & Kraus LLP, did not issue formal denials of coverage but reserved all rights under their respective policies, asserting that their excess layers would not be reached based on the application of the named-windstorm sub-limit asserted by Ironclad and Pinnacle.

**E.** On March 1, 2023, VHG filed a multi-count complaint in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, in and for Miami-Dade County, captioned *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corp., Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc., Montclair Assurance Company, and Sovereign Re Ltd.*, Case No. 2022-CA-031547, assigned to the Honorable Catherine Embry, Circuit Judge (the \"Litigation\"). In the Litigation, VHG asserted claims for: (i) breach of contract against all four Insurer Parties; (ii) declaratory judgment seeking a judicial determination of coverage rights under the Policies; and (iii) bad faith, including both statutory bad faith under Section 624.155 of the Florida Statutes and common-law bad faith, against all four Insurer Parties. VHG\'s complaint alleged total business-interruption losses of approximately Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000), comprised of approximately Thirty-One Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$31,400,000) attributable to the Verimark Grand Key Resort, approximately Eighteen Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$18,700,000) attributable to the Verimark Harborview Hotel & Conference Center, and approximately Nine Million Nine Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$9,900,000) attributable to the Verimark Sunset Shores. On April 15, 2023, Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re, through their respective counsel, filed answers and affirmative defenses denying liability and raising numerous defenses to VHG\'s claims. Thereafter, the Parties conducted extensive fact discovery, including the exchange of voluminous documents, written discovery, and depositions of party representatives, including depositions of VHG\'s Chief Executive Officer Marcus Ellsworth, VHG\'s Chief Financial Officer Diane Calder, VHG\'s General Counsel Nathaniel Driscoll, Ironclad\'s Senior Vice President of Claims Victor Haddon, and Arbor Claims Services LLC\'s lead adjuster Denise Whitford. The Parties also conducted expert discovery, including the retention a... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

**F.** On December 4 and December 5, 2023, the Parties participated in a two-day mediation session before the Honorable Richard Mendelson (Ret.) of Keystone Dispute Resolution Inc. in Miami, Florida. All Parties appeared through their respective counsel and authorized corporate representatives with full settlement authority. At the conclusion of the mediation on December 5, 2023, the Parties reached an agreement in principle to resolve all disputes and claims among them, which agreement in principle was memorialized in a binding term sheet executed by all Parties on that date. The Parties subsequently negotiated the terms of this Agreement to memorialize the final and comprehensive terms of their settlement.

**G.** The Parties desire to fully and finally resolve any and all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, disputes, and controversies between and among them arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies, without any admission of liability, fault, or wrongdoing by any Party, and on the terms and conditions set forth herein.
